minutes.headline: Select Board approved the Unifier roots gathering entertainment license and honored retiring member Alonso
minutes.summary: The meeting opened with public comment on reuse of town buildings and green space, then tributes to retiring selectman Alonso at his last meeting. The state delegation described the House and Senate budgets and uncertainty over state and federal revenue. The board discussed a street-cut moratorium policy, approved a conditional entertainment license, returned a liquor license to its prior holder, heard reports and a quarterly revenue update, and went into executive session.

what_happened.line: The Select Board approved a conditional entertainment event at 300 Holman Street; the vote was not audible in the captions.
The town manager is to bring a fee schedule amendment and a specific license proposal for the event to the next agenda.
The board returned the Hadwin Market liquor license to the seller; the vote was not audible in the captions.
The DPW director is to revise the pavement cut moratorium draft with notification and exemption wording, and Town Counsel is to review it.
The meeting opened with tributes to retiring member Alonso, and the state delegation described the state budget and uncertain revenue.

why_it_matters: A pavement cut moratorium would set when utility and private work can open newly paved streets, and its notification and exemption terms are still being written.
The event approval depends on a new fee schedule amendment, and a rain barrel and compost bundle sold below cost would draw on a revolving fund, so both return to the agenda before any action.
The teacher contract and uncertain state aid bear on future school budgets and on the town budget, mostly taxes.
watch_next: The June 6th meeting, where a tabled agenda item is due to return.
The next agenda: the fee schedule amendment and license proposal for the entertainment event, and the revised pavement cut moratorium draft.
